record.context_brief: Compactness of convex hulls in CAT(0)
record.original_question: Let X be a complete length CAT(0) space, not assumed locally compact, and let K be a compact subset of X. Is the closed convex hull of K, meaning the intersection of all closed convex subsets of X that contain K, necessarily compact?

evidence.quote: Let X be a geodesic metric space. Recall that, a set C ⊂ X is called convex if, for any two points x, y ∈ C, every geodesic from x to y lies in C. The closed convex hull of a subset K ⊂ X is defined as the intersection of all closed convex sets containing K.
Let K be a compact subset in a complete length CAT(0) space X. Is it true that the closed convex hull of K is compact?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A geodesic metric space is a metric space $(X,d)$ in which every two points are joined by a (not necessarily unique) geodesic, i.e. an isometric embedding of a closed interval $[0,L]\subset\mathbb{R}$ whose endpoints are the given two points. A geodesic metric space $X$ is called CAT(0) if every geodesic triangle in $X$ is at least as thin as its Euclidean comparison triangle: explicitly, for any three points $p,q,r\in X$ and any choice of geodesics between them forming a triangle $\Delta$, and for any two points $x,y$ on the sides of $\Delta$, one has $d(x,y)\le d_{\mathbb{R}^2}(\bar x,\bar y)$, where $\bar x,\bar y$ are the corresponding points on a Euclidean comparison triangle $\bar\Delta\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ with the same side lengths as $\Delta$. A subset $C\subset X$ is convex if for every $x,y\in C$, every geodesic in $X$ from $x$ to $y$ lies in $C$. For a subset $K\subset X$, the closed convex hull $\overline{\mathrm{conv}}(K)$ is the intersection of all closed convex subsets of $X$ that contain $K$. Assume $X$ is a complete length CAT(0) space (no local compactness or properness assumed) and let $K\subset X$ be a compact subset.

Question: Is $\overline{\mathrm{conv}}(K)$ necessarily compact?
artifact.status_search_result: The question (attributed to Gromov) is widely regarded as open in the general (non-proper) setting. It is known to hold when $X$ is proper (locally compact complete CAT(0)), and reduces to the case of finite sets $K$, but even the three-point case is open. Recent work has produced counterexamples in weaker non-positively curved settings (spaces with conical geodesic bicombings), where the closed convex hull of finitely many points need not be compact, but the original CAT(0) question remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Compact sets and the closure of their convex hulls in CAT(0) spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Studies Gromov's question on whether the closed convex hull of a compact set in a complete CAT(0) space is compact; affirmative in proper case, reduces to finite sets, three-point case open.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is widely cited as an open question of Gromov, with only partial results (proper spaces, flat CAT(0), reduction to finite sets).

status_evidence.title: A non-compact convex hull in generalized non-positive curvature
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs a complete metric space with a conical geodesic bicombing that is the closed convex hull of finitely many points yet is non-compact.
status_evidence.claim: Counterexamples exist in weaker non-positive curvature settings, but the CAT(0) version remains open.
